text: Here is a square wave. Flat tops, sharp corners.
So how do you roll it out of circles?
Follow its tip. Its height draws a sine wave.
Hang a smaller one on its tip: three times as fast, a third the size.
Then a fifth, a seventh, odd ones only, until the wave is square.
But look closely at a corner.
There's a spike. Add more circles, and it only gets thinner.
It never gets shorter. About nine percent, every time.
asr: It never gets shorter, about 9% every time.

text: Even infinitely many circles leave it there. It's called the Gibbs phenomenon.
